October 20, 2026





The 100+ page guide to orchestrating LLM workflows*



Your LLM workflow works in a notebook. Now it needs scheduling, retries, monitoring, and a way to ask for human review. This 100+ page guide shows how Apache Airflow brings those pieces together, with practical patterns and code examples for LLM tasks and agents. Free to download.
*Message from this week's sponsor, Astronomer



 

 

 

Posts & Tutorials



 

 

🔗 Note: if you don’t see links in this email, it’s also available on the web: dataelixir.com/archive/issue-594.html



 

Fifty years of the data stack



Today’s data stack makes more sense when you see how we got here. This interactive timeline traces 50 years of analytical systems, showing how database access, query engines, and storage evolved together, and why older technologies still sit alongside newer ones.
Columnar | Ian Cook



 

How to be more ambitious: A tutorial for humans with models



Most people use AI to do familiar tasks faster, but Felix Rieseberg argues we're thinking too small. In this post, he explores three ways to be more ambitious, with practical advice and concrete examples.
Felix Rieseberg



 

Can you use autoregressive diffusion to generate market data?



Jane Street tried using diffusion models to generate realistic streams of stock market events but it turns out that the market data's mixture of continuous values and discrete actions makes this difficult. This research write-up explores what worked, what didn't, and what the experiments revealed about generative modeling.
Jane Street Blog | James Somers



 

Better Context, Better Answers



Better business context can matter more than a better model. In AtScale’s preliminary benchmark results, adding a semantic layer improved accuracy more than switching models. Join AtScale and analyst Andrew Brust on October 28 at 2 pm ET to examine the comparisons and learn how to test whether AI gets your business numbers right.
// sponsored

Data Visualization



 

 

Dogs of New York



nycdogs is an R package containing New York City's dog licensing and dog bite data. It's great for teaching because the datasets are large, messy, and full of interesting things to explore. Besides, everyone loves dogs. In this post, Kieran Healy explores the data and shows how duplicate records, messy zip codes, and missing information can complicate even simple questions.
Kieran Healy



 

Dual axes, not dueling



Every dual-axis chart has an implied exchange rate between its two scales, and that choice can change the story the chart tells. In this post, RJ Andrews uses animated examples and historical charts to explain when dual axes are misleading, when they're useful, and what works better.
dbt Charts | RJ Andrews



 

 

 

Trends



 

 

30 Months on the Exponential (in Charts)



“This is the worst AI you'll ever use.”
One Useful Thing | Ethan Mollick



 

 

 

Tools & Code



 

 

Python 3.15 for Data Scientists



Python 3.15 is here, with some useful improvements for data scientists. This practical walkthrough covers lazy imports for faster startup, immutable dictionaries for safer configurations, and a new profiler that can find bottlenecks in running code. Includes examples, benchmarks, and visualizations.
Khuyen Tran



 

Frisket



Frisket is an open-source AI spreadsheet that turns unstructured information into data you can easily work with. Load PDFs, emails, audio, or video, then extract, classify, and analyze the contents in a familiar spreadsheet interface. It supports local AI models, so you can even run the whole thing privately.
Jonathan Soma



 

 

 

Outlier



 

 

 Tiny Charts: Data Viz as Postage Stamp Art



This is a great deep dive into how countries use data visualization to communicate national priorities, economic growth, and scientific progress on... postage stamps. There are 180 examples here spanning decades of this unusual genre, along with a spreadsheet of the entire collection.
Nightingale | Julie Peasley

October 13, 2026





Earn your Master of Translational Data Analytics online from The Ohio State University*



Transform data into insights with the online Master of Translational Data Analytics from Ohio State’s Translational Data Analytics Institute. This interdisciplinary program blends machine learning, user experience, data visualization, and design thinking to prepare you to uncover and present insights from data.
*Message from this week's sponsor, The Ohio State University



 

 

Trends



 

 

State of AI Report 2026



This slide deck is one of the most comprehensive overviews you'll find about the current state of AI. It highlights developments in research, industry, policy, and safety, plus predictions for the coming year. It’s dense, but the slide format makes it easy to browse.
Nathan Benaich and Air Street Capital



 

 

 

Posts & Tutorials



 

 

🔗 Note: if you don’t see links in this email, it’s also available on the web: dataelixir.com/archive/issue-593.html



 

7 Statistical Rules of Thumb: How Good Are They?



Statistical rules of thumb are easy to remember but for them to be useful, you need to know when to trust them. In this post, Jim Frost walks through seven familiar shortcuts, including the rule of 30 and the 80/20 principle, explaining where they come from, when they help, and how much confidence they deserve.
Jim Frost



 

A DuckDB Database with No Data in It



A DuckDB database doesn't need to hold any data to be useful. This walkthrough shows how to store a database of views that point to remote Parquet files, which essentially turns it into a tiny, shared catalog. Users get ready-to-query datasets through a single URL, while the data stays where it is.
The DuckDB team



 

How TABLESAMPLE picks rows



Sampling can make a query much faster, but it matters how you pick the rows. In this post, Radim Marek explains PostgreSQL’s sampling options, why nearby rows can give you less information than you expect, and how to build consistent samples that still work across related tables.
Radim Marek



 

Benchmarking the Future of Work



AI can now outperform licensed accountants on certain detailed accounting tasks, but that doesn’t mean it can do the whole job. Using tasks adapted from APEX-Accounting, Mercor explores what these results suggest about the future of work and the growing importance of communication, context, and asking the right questions.
// sponsored

Data Visualization



 

 

Tufte's Razor - A guide to the data-ink ratio



Edward Tufte’s data-ink ratio encourages people to remove chart elements that don’t convey information, but how far should you go? This interactive guide lets you adjust bars, labels, and other details to see what makes a chart more clear and what gets lost along the way.
Science UX | Tufte's Razor



 

ggindex



Sometimes a few points on a chart need more explanation than a short label can provide. ggindex is a new ggplot2 extension that marks those points with numbers and puts their descriptions in a matching legend. That gives you room to explain them without crowding the chart.
Discindo



 

 

 

Tools & Code



 

 

Release of Polars 2.0



Polars 2.0 brings some useful changes for everyday data work, including streaming by default, the ability to spill some operations to disk when memory runs short, and expanded SQL support. If you’re upgrading, check the migration guide, especially if your analysis depends on row order.
Polars | Ritchie Vink



 

An explosion of R package and environment managers



R has several new tools for managing packages and environments and it can be hard to keep them straight. In this post, Isabella Velásquez explains how five options differ, with examples for sharing a project, recreating its software environment, or making a single script easier to rerun.
R Works | Isabella Velásquez



 

 

 

Outlier



 

 



Weather Ribbon



This new site compresses climate charts into visual summaries for cities around the world. Click through for city-specific pages that show 30-year climate normals, covering things like temperature, precipitation, humidity, cloud cover, wind, and more. The code is open-source and it's a nice example of clean visual design.
Weather Ribbon

Real-Time Personalization*



Building a model is one thing. Using its decisions and checking its work is another. In this webinar, Snowplow and Conductrics will build predictive audiences from real time behavioral data, show how to constrain the model, and bring its decisions back into your data for analysis. If you can't make the time, sign up for the recording!
*Message from this week's sponsor, Snowplow



 

 

 

Posts & Tutorials



 

 

🔗 Note: if you don’t see links in this email, it’s also available on the web: dataelixir.com/archive/issue-592.html



 

R and Python and the Holy Grail



If you use Python for modeling and R for exploring results and making figures, it helps to have both on equal footing. This walkthrough shows how to use both in Positron, with a shared conda environment and a remote setup that keeps the work where the data live.
Mike Talbot



 

Language Models for Text Classification: From Bag-of-Words to Jev



There are a variety of ways to classify text, from logistic regression to prompting an LLM. This is a great guide to how those approaches work, where a decision model like Jev fits, and the tradeoffs between training your own classifier and using a model that handles different tasks out of the box.
Ahead of AI | Sebastian Raschka, PhD



 

Signals and Systems Principles for Data Scientists



This collection of interactive lessons turns the most useful parts of a classic signals and systems textbook into 16 self-contained labs on smoothing, sampling, stability, frequency response, and other ideas that show up in real data work.
regrok | Vipin Gupta



 

What a p-value tells you, and what it does not



Repeat the same experiment with the same real effect, and you can get a tiny p-value one time and an unremarkable one the next. This simulation-based walkthrough shows how that happens and why the confidence interval tells you more than the p-value does.
Tidy Ecology

Tools & Code



 

 

Ledge



Ledge is an open-source Markdown notebook with code execution built in. Each note gets its own persistent shell and code blocks can run locally or over SSH. It supports Python, SQL, a CLI, and an MCP server for agents to read and update your notes.
ledge.sh



 

R Workspaces as Static Websites



webrarian is a new R package that turns a folder of R scripts and data into a static website where users can run and edit the code in their browsers. That makes it easy to share an analysis because there’s nothing for users to install and no compute server to maintain.
James Balamuta



 

 

 

Outlier



 

 

How Autumn (Foliage) Is Measured



This is a fun rabbit hole about how people measure autumn, from volunteers watching individual trees to satellites tracking entire forests, and why deciding when the colors are “at peak” is harder than it sounds.
Counting Stuff | Randy Au
